answer: Reverse-Reputation Entry Cost. Each new identity starts at a vertex score of zero and must earn its first payout only after 30 days of sustained, rate-limited work; until then every action costs a small fee that is refunded only on completion. A clone farm therefore pays full operating cost across the entire dawn period with no revenue, while its eventual reward is diluted by the same reputation curve. An atlas of verified histories is unnecessary: the ledger itself records the delay, making each marginal clone strictly negative-EV.
